caption: Sherrill v. Knight
court: United States Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
holding:
The D.C. Circuit held that the protection the First Amendment gives to newsgathering requires that White House press access not be denied arbitrarily or for less than compelling reasons, and that due process requires "notice of the factual bases for denial, an opportunity for the applicant to respond to these, and a final written statement of the reasons for denial."{c:13}{c:14}{c:15}{c:16}

Status as of 2026-09-22: Final.{c:13}{c:14}{c:15}{c:16}

caption: Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump
court: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
holding:
Judge Timothy J. Kelly granted CNN a temporary restraining order requiring the White House to reinstate Jim Acosta's hard pass, on due process grounds drawn from Sherrill v. Knight. The White House restored the pass and CNN dropped the suit.{c:17}{c:18}{c:19}

Status as of 2026-09-22: Dismissed.{c:17}{c:18}{c:19}

caption: Associated Press v. Budowich
court: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia; U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
holding:
The district court (Judge Trevor N. McFadden, 2025-04-08) granted a preliminary injunction ordering AP's access restored and then stayed it pending appeal. A D.C. Circuit panel (Judges Pillard, Katsas and Rao, 2025-06-06) granted a partial stay, 2 to 1, holding that the Oval Office, Air Force One, Mar-a-Lago and the Cabinet Room are restricted spaces where access is a matter of presidential discretion, and leaving AP's East Room access in place; Judge Pillard dissented. The full D.C. Circuit denied rehearing en banc on 2025-07-22.{c:20}{c:21}{c:22}{c:23}

Status as of 2026-09-22: On appeal.{c:20}{c:21}{c:22}{c:23}
